title: NFR-004 Recovery: a worker killed mid-workflow resumes from checkpoint without duplicating
risk: A crashed worker either loses the in-flight action so the customer never receives it, or restarts from the beginning and duplicates the already-sent message or order.
preconditions: Namespace gov-nfr-<case_id>-<worker_id>; NFR verification runs against the offline gateway with mock SoR and channel boundaries.
Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; failure, outage and crash injections are scripted at the substituted boundary, never faked inside the assertion.
A real worker process is started against the offline gateway so it can be terminated and restarted.

steps.action: Start the workflow and let it reach the composed step
steps.expected: Steps 1 to 3 are checkpointed with their outputs persisted; no outbound effect exists yet.

steps.action: Terminate the worker process (SIGKILL) and confirm the lease expires or is reclaimed
steps.expected: The run is reclaimed by another worker after lease expiry; the interrupted run is marked interrupted rather than completed.

steps.action: Restart the worker and let recovery proceed
steps.expected: Recovery resumes at the send step using the checkpointed composition; the adapter receives exactly one send.

steps.action: Seed a second failure: kill the worker after the send but before the record step
steps.expected: On restart the persisted receipt for the effect_key prevents a second send, and the record step completes.

assertions: Work resumes from the last checkpoint instead of restarting the whole workflow.
Exactly one external effect exists in both kill scenarios.
The interrupted run is never reported as completed before its final step succeeded.
Recovery is driven by persisted state, so a second worker can complete the run.
forbidden: Re-executing steps that already produced an external effect.
Marking the run completed when the worker died mid-step.
Keeping checkpoints only in the dead process memory.
evidence: Worker logs around each kill with the lease transitions.
Checkpoint records and the single adapter send receipt.
Run state history including the interrupted state.
cleanup: Stop any worker started by the case, delete gov- execution and checkpoint rows, and confirm no lease remains.
automation: Real worker process and durable checkpoint/lease logic under test: the crash is an actual process termination, not a simulated exception, so in-memory-only implementations fail.
prerequisites: Requires the runnable offline harness (worker process + Postgres/Redis substitutes). Without it the case is SKIP_UNIMPLEMENTED, never PASS.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
